sections.overview: Teleocichla cinderella is a freshwater cichlid described from the lower Tocantins River in Brazil.
sections.identification: It is a small, elongated member of a genus adapted to life in fast-flowing water.
sections.habitat: The genus is associated with rapids and other strong-current habitats; the species’ type locality was at Tucuruí on the Tocantins.
sections.diet: Species-specific diet details are not given in the primary description or summary sources consulted.
sections.behavior: Its rheophilic body form is associated with life in flowing water, but detailed behavior is poorly documented.
sections.reproduction: The sources consulted do not provide reliable species-specific breeding information.
sections.ecology: Its known distribution is restricted to the lower Tocantins basin, where fast-water habitat has been heavily altered by dams.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports the 2018 global IUCN assessment as Endangered.
